newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Balladur warns against early retirement.
newsitem.headline: France's Balladur warns against early retirement.

text.p: Former Prime Minister Edouard Balladur warned on Sunday against a reduction in retirement age from 60 to 55, saying it would worsen the unemployment situation in France.
Economic and demographic realities instead may in the future push back retirement age, he said.
"This (early retirement) would not create jobs. This would worsen unemployment," Balladur said in an interview on TF1 television.

"Today one cannot in France consider a reduction in the retirement age. French people must be told that in the future we may be forced to raise it (retirement age) and not reduce it," Balladur told TF1's public affairs programme "7/7."
In November, the French government gave in to truckers' demands for retirement at age 55 after they staged a 12-day strike that crippled the country.
Some unions want that right extended to other workers.
Balladur, who lost the last presidential election to Jacques Chirac, also reiterated calls for a bolder economic policy to fight unemployment and boost growth.

"I think it (government policy) goes in the right direction. But it must be slightly changed, towards further tax cuts, a more flexible monetary policy and a social policy that provides the means needed to lower unemployment," he said.
